The '''Colorado Group''' was an Australian company that operated retail clothing and footwear chains. Major brands include Colorado Adventurewear, Mathers, Williams the Shoemen, [[JAG (clothing)|JAG]], Diana Ferrari and Pairs. The company was based in [[Brisbane]].

__TOC__
==History==
The history of the Colorado Group dates back to the 1864 founding of Williams the Shoemen in [[Ballarat]]. In 1999 it was listed on the [[Australian Securities Exchange]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20080718180142/http://www.coloradogroup.com.au/content.aspx?pageID=20&mainID=18|title=Corporate History}} Colorado Group</ref>

In May 2007, ARH Investments launched a successful [[takeover offer]].<ref>[https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20070517/pdf/312hzhyvqkrp9c.pdf Takeover bid by ARH Investments (Australia ) Pty Ltd for Colorado Group Ltd] Colorado Group 17 May 2007</ref> Colorado was delisted from the Australian Securities Exchange on 15 August 2007.<ref>[https://www.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20070815/pdf/313zd0ht01bnkj.pdf Colorado Group Limited Removal from Official List] [[Australian Securities Exchange]] 15 August 2007</ref>

As at June 2011 Colorado had 434 stores in Australia and New Zealand, and employed 3,800 people. It owed around $400 million to 18 financiers.<ref name="shuts 1042 jobs" />

The Colorado clothing retail group went into receivership on 30 March 2011.<ref>{{cite news|last=Janda|first=Michael|title=Colorado Group for sale|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2011/04/05/3183022.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409071911/http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2011/04/05/3183022.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 April 2011|accessdate=14 June 2011|newspaper=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]]|date=5 April 2011}}</ref> [[Ferrier Hodgson]] was appointed administrator.<ref name=closing>{{cite news|last=Butler|first=Ben|title=Retailer Colorado to close, jobs to go|url=http://www.smh.com.au/business/retailer-colorado-to-close-jobs-to-go-20110614-1g21f.html|accessdate=14 June 2011|newspaper=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=15 June 2011}}</ref> Colorado was owned by [[Affinity Equity Partners]].<ref name=closing/> In 2011, the company became known as Fusion Retail Brands.

In June 2011 it was announced that the clothing chain was to close with the loss of 1,042 jobs.<ref name=closing/> In Australia, 100 underperforming Colorado stores shut, 21 Williams stores, seven Mathers stores, two JAG stores and one Diana Ferrari store.<ref name="shuts 1042 jobs">{{cite news|title=Colorado shuts the doors on 1042 jobs|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/news/breaking-news/plus-jobs-to-go-in-colorado-closures/story-e6frf7ko-1226075162418|accessdate=14 June 2011|newspaper=[[Herald Sun]]|date=14 June 2011|agency=AAP}}</ref> In [[New South Wales]] 42 stores closed, and in [[Victoria, Australia|Victoria]] 27 closed.<ref name=closing/> Nine Colorado Stores in New Zealand also closed.<ref name="shuts 1042 jobs"/>

Colorado ceased selling its clothing lines, returning to its beginning as a shoe brand which were sold through the company's Mathers and Williams the Shoemen stores, and online.<ref name=closing/> In September 2013, the JAG brand was sold to Apparel Group.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 September 2013 |title=Apparel Group acquires JAG |url=https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/apparel-group-acquires-jag |access-date=2023-09-19 |website=Ragtrader |language=en}}</ref>

In 2014, Couper Finance purchased Fusion Retail Brands,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Sarah |last2=Macdonald |first2=Anthony |last3=Friemann |first3=Gretchen |date=2014-01-07 |title=Fusion Retail Brands strikes deal with Couper Finance |url=https://www.afr.com/policy/fusion-retail-brands-strikes-deal-with-couper-finance-20140108-ij99n |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-09-19 |website=[[Australian Financial Review]]|language=en}}</ref> then, in 2017, Munro Footwear Group purchased Fusion Retail Brands from Couper Finance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Sue |date=2017-06-29 |title=Fusion Retail right fit for Munro Footwear |url=https://www.afr.com/companies/retail/fusion-retail-right-fit-for-munro-footwear-20170628-gx01dt |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-09-19 |website=Australian Financial Review |language=en}}</ref>
